newsitem.title: JAPAN: French poll result boosts mark in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: French poll result boosts mark in Tokyo.

text.p: An unexpected lead by left-wing parties in a French parliamentary election pushed up the mark against other major units in Tokyo on Monday as traders grew cautious about France's commitment to a single European currency.

The opposition Socialists, Communists, extreme-left and other left-wing candidates took a surprising lead over the ruling coalition and other moderate-right candidates in Sunday's first round vote in the election for the 577-seat National Assembly.
"It was something we did not expect," said Hidemitsu Terry Terasawa, manager of the foreign exchange and treasury division at the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd.
Traders said the market got even more nervous after seeing details of the results, which showed an increase in votes won by Communists, the extreme-right and other fringe parties.
"What I am concerned with is that Communists and the extreme-right (National Front) are receiving more votes," said Nobuo Kihara, forex marketing head at Banque Paribas in Tokyo.

The mark was bought after the market saw the good performance by parties which are not particularly eager to meet the tough fiscal goals necessary for joining the European economic and monetary union, he added.

Traders said the prospect of a leftist win in the second round of voting on June 1 cast doubts over the smooth passage of the EMU and supported the German currency, seen as a stronger currency on its own, against other European units.

The mark rose to around 3.3760 French francs just after news of the opposition's lead emerged around 1800 GMT on Sunday. The mark was quoted at 3.3765/68 francs at 0520 GMT, up from 3.3695/00 in late Friday trading in Europe.
But some dealers said a win by left-wing French parties would be a minus for the single European currency overall and eventually would prompt dollar buying against the mark.
"If France and others move to ease criteria to enter the Euro, that would prompt dollar buying against the mark, although Germany would oppose such an idea," said a dealer at a European bank.

In mark/yen trades, the unexpected poll result and expectations of political uncertainty in France encouraged traders to cover short positions in marks against the yen, which indirectly pushed up the dollar versus the yen.
The German currency was quoted at 69.02/05 yen at 0520 GMT, up from 68.25 yen at the New York close on Friday.
But the mark's buoyancy during the Asian session was partly limited by talk that the Bank of France may be placing offers above 3.3750 French francs, traders said.

"Traders are waiting for the final result of the poll on June 1. But there is no incentive to buy and hold French francs right now, given that French bonds and stocks are likely to fall in response," BOT-Mitsubishi's Terasawa said.
French financial futures markets tumbled in early Monday pre-session GLOBEX electronic trading, with June PIBOR falling 25 basis points and June bond futures falling as much as 0.70 to 128.30.
Dealers were anxious to see how traders in Paris would react to the latest poll results later on Monday, saying that the news has not yet been fully digested in the market.
But some said the impact on currencies may be limited on Monday, with London and New York markets closed for a holiday.
As for the second ballot, Tokyo dealers had mixed views on whether the left-wing parties would be able to keep their substantial lead.
"It is also possible that the ruling coalItion will come from behind to clinch victory, so it is hard to take heavy positions either way," a dealer at a French bank said.
